chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, all from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from a man, from Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him), that he said:
Regarding the woman whose husband dies and he had not entered (consummated marriage) with her, indeed for her is half the dower, and for her is the inheritance, and upon her is the waiting period.
ai.seo_question: What are the rights of a widow if her husband died before consummating the marriage?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi, transmitted through the chain of Ibn Abi Umayr, clarifies the tripartite legal status of a widow whose husband died prior to consummation, distinguishing it from cases of divorce. It affirms that she retains full inheritance rights and the obligation of iddah, while receiving half the stipulated dower, a ruling consistent with the principle that death triggers full inheritance but partial dower due to the absence of sexual union. This specific ruling is foundational in Shia fiqh for resolving disputes regarding financial settlements in early widowhood.
